name: thorn tree

attributes.attribute: must not be cut on May 11 or November 11
in a group of three signals fairy activity

sources: Briggs, Katherine M. The Folklore of the Cotswolds. London: B. T. Batsford Ltd., 1974, 120.
Spence, Lewis. The Minor Traditions of British Mythology. (New York: Benjamin Blom, Inc., 1972), 108.
Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The thorn tree is one of the most powerful and magical plants in Celtic lands. It grows in several species, chiefly the blackthorn and the whitethorn. The blackthorn blooms each spring near the feast of Beltane on May 1. Beside its pale white blooms sit sharp needles of wood. These can easily pierce the flesh. The tree was used mainly as a cattle hedge. But its magic mattered more, for it protected people against the fairies. It had to be tended with care so it would not lose that power. No one should cut thorn trees on May 11 or November 11. The trees would take vengeance on the woodsman. The whitethorn likewise sheltered people. But its wood had to stay out of doors. Fairies could sense it indoors and would haunt the house. A thorn that grew with an ash and an oak was a sure sign of fairy activity nearby.

okr.objective: Record the thorn tree as a protective and magical plant.
